key_insight: NEO-ov demonstrates that a native, end-to-end 'one-vision' foundation model can preserve pixel-level signals across frames and directly map pixels to words at scale, enabling multi-image, video and spatial reasoning without stitching separate image encoders and language decoders.
problem_solved: Existing modular vision–language pipelines fragment pixel information across processing stages and limit early pixel–word interactions; native VLMs have been strong on single images but underexplored and unscaled for multi-image, video and spatial tasks. NEO-ov addresses this gap by providing a unified, scalable native model for cross-frame multimodal understanding.
method: Design a unified native architecture that ingests raw pixels from one or multiple images/frames and produces language tokens end-to-end (pixels → words) without separate encoder/decoder modules.
Use cross-frame spatial–temporal attention and positional encodings to maintain pixel-to-word alignment and enable interactions across frames/regions.

Scale training with multi-task pretraining (captioning, VQA, grounding-like objectives) and efficiency-focused design choices (patching/tokenization and attention optimizations) to support large-scale multimodal learning.
impact: Simplifies VLM pipelines and improves early pixel–word interactions, enabling stronger video, multi-image and spatial reasoning capabilities for applications like video QA, embodied AI, retrieval and visual grounding. Practitioners can build more coherent, end-to-end multimodal systems with fewer hand-off artifacts and better spatio-temporal alignment.
visual_elements: Architecture flowchart: raw pixels (multi-frame) → native transformer with cross-frame attention → language outputs (captions/answers).
Side-by-side comparison: modular pipeline (separate encoder + decoder) vs native one-vision model (unified, end-to-end) highlighting where pixel–word interactions occur.
Attention maps over consecutive frames showing preserved pixel alignment and cross-frame references.
Application panel: example use cases (video QA, multi-image captioning, spatial grounding) with before/after outputs.
paper_title: From Pixels to Words -- Towards Native One-Vision Models at Scale
paper_authors: Haiwen Diao, Jiahao Wang, Penghao Wu, Yuhao Dong, Yuwei Niu
